verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light on anyway,
burning for no one,
all through the empty afternoon.

verses.author: model_A
model_B
verses.text:
Someone counts the change left in a jar,
enough for one more month, maybe,
while rain decides not to stop today.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The mail carrier learns the new names slowly,
tucking flyers into a box
that no longer answers back.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone plants tomatoes anyway,
not for this summer's table,
but for whoever comes after asking why.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A child finds the old key in the grass,
tries every lock in the neighborhood,
keeps it anyway when none of them fit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The bus stops running at nine now,
so we learn the shape of walking home,
counting porch lights instead of minutes.
